_note: LA ARBOLEDA, as data. Every species the world can plant, keyed by the name the world emits. `form` picks which painter in src/render/c2d/flora.js builds the silhouette — the FORMS are code (they are geometry), the species are not. Adding a tree is a row here plus, at most, a mix that names it. Palettes run dark body -> mid -> highlight, the one lighting idiom every plant in this world shares.

forms.broadleaf: the shared canopy stack: a round, slightly ragged crown on a short trunk
forms.conifer: stacked tiers narrowing upward — a cone read from above with its shadow side
forms.column: one tall narrow crown: a cypress is a vertical line in a landscape
forms.bare: trunk and branches, no canopy — the dry season, and what a dead tree looks like
forms.palm: a leaning trunk under a ring of fronds — a palm is a different tree and has to stay one
forms.mangrove: a dense low crown over a cage of prop roots, standing in the tide

almendro.note: the default, and what every tree in this world was until now

guanacaste.note: the national tree: a huge low crown much wider than it is tall

cortez.note: cortez amarillo in bloom — the dry season's yellow, and the only tree here that is not green

seco.note: dry-season bare, or dead. No crown at all — the silhouette IS the branches

pino.note: highland. Not a Puntarenas coastal tree — zoned inland, toward the cordillera

cipres.note: highland, and a vertical: it reads at a glance because nothing else here is tall and narrow

cerezo.note: el cerezo en flor. Ornamental and deliberately not native — it is pink, it is meant to be found

palma.note: la palma: the Paseo median, the beaches and the faro. Its palette was the ALMENDRO'S until now — the same array, shared by import, so recolouring one tree silently recoloured every frond in the world

mangle.note: el mangle: the darkest green in this world, but the same ramp as every other crown. Drawn by ground.js, which imported the almendro's palette to get it

mixes._note: Which species a wood plants, and how often. Weights need not sum to 1 — they are normalised. `d` is px² of ground per tree, so a bigger number is a thinner wood. `floor` is the wash laid under a wood — bare land tan under trees reads as a beach with trees on it.

seco.note: tropical dry forest: the coast and the estero's far shore

monte.note: the ordinary green hinterland between the coast and the hills

altura.note: the cordillera behind the port: denser, darker, and where the cerezos are
